sections.content:
This stage is the information-and-capability foundation used by Agentic Studio. It does not simply give an LLM 'more data'. It creates six controlled planes: Knowledge Base for authoritative source material; RAG for semantic retrieval; Knowledge Graph for relationships and topology; Telemetry for time-sensitive operational state; Models for evaluated predictive/analytical capabilities; and Tools for bounded actions.

The design principle is: knowledge informs, telemetry contextualizes, models estimate, tools act, and the Agent SPEC + Policy decide what the Runtime is allowed to do.

AGENT SPEC                        |                        v                  AGENT RUNTIME                        |        +---------------+----------------+        |       CONTEXT ORCHESTRATOR     |        +---+---------+--------+---------+            |         |        |            RAG       KG    TELEMETRY            |         |        |           KB     topology   live state            |         |        |            +---------+--------+                      |                    MODELS                      |                 typed proposal                      |                    TOOLS                      |                Tool Gateway                      |                INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

sections.heading_text: 2. Why Six Components Instead of One Vector Database
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-015 > 2. Why Six Components Instead of One Vector Database
sections.content: A vector index alone cannot reliably represent current asset state, causal/structural relationships, authorization, or executable capabilities. AI-ConneX therefore treats retrieval, graph traversal, telemetry, inference and action as different contracts.
tables:
| Need | Primary source | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authoritative documents | Knowledge Base | Preserves source/version/authority |
| Semantic similarity | RAG | Finds relevant passages |
| Relationships/topology | Knowledge Graph | Answers connected questions |
| Current machine state | Telemetry | Provides time-sensitive evidence |
| Prediction/estimation | Models | Computes learned outputs |
| Side effects | Tools | Executes explicit capabilities |

sections.content:
Industrial agents need answers that are simultaneously relevant, attributable, structurally correct, current, and actionable. Research therefore focuses on preventing five common substitutions: using similarity for truth, documents for live state, graph edges for causal certainty, model predictions for authorization, and tools as unrestricted functions.

Can retrieval be grounded to authoritative, versioned sources?

Can graph relationships complement semantic retrieval without becoming a hallucination amplifier?

Can live telemetry be freshness-aware and separated from static knowledge?

Can models be consumed through strict input/output contracts?

Can tools be capability-limited and policy-enforced?

Can all evidence and actions be traced to the exact agent execution?

Authority is explicit: source authority is metadata, not inferred from similarity.

Freshness is explicit: telemetry has timestamps, quality and maximum age.

Relationships are explicit: graph edges carry provenance and confidence.

Models are not authorities: predictions require model/version and context.

Tools are not knowledge: a tool is a capability with a schema and side-effect classification.

Untrusted retrieved text cannot change policy, permissions or SPEC.

Every result carries provenance sufficient for replay and audit.

Tenant/site/asset scope is applied before retrieval, graph traversal, inference or tool execution.

sections.content:
The Knowledge Base is the authoritative source layer. It stores or references manuals, SOPs, maintenance records, engineering specifications, standards, incident reports, approved procedures and other governed material.

A KB record is not automatically trusted simply because it is indexed. Approval state, scope and provenance are evaluated before retrieval results become usable evidence.
tables:
| KB metadata | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| document_uid | Stable identity |
| version | Exact revision |
| authority_level | Source trust classification |
| owner | Responsible organization |
| effective_from/to | Validity period |
| asset/site scope | Applicability |
| classification | Security/access level |
| checksum | Integrity |
| source_uri | Original location |
| approval_state | Draft/approved/retired |
| language | Retrieval/indexing |

sections.content:
SOURCE  -> connector  -> malware/file validation  -> parser/OCR  -> metadata extraction  -> classification  -> access-control tagging  -> chunking  -> embedding  -> lexical index  -> vector index  -> provenance registry  -> approval  -> published collection

Never overwrite a published document version; create a new immutable version.

Hash source content before processing.

Retain page/section/table identifiers where possible.

Mark obsolete documents as retired rather than deleting provenance.

Apply tenant and asset scope during ingestion, not only at query time.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the evidence-retrieval mechanism. AI-ConneX uses hybrid retrieval rather than treating embeddings as the sole truth mechanism: lexical retrieval handles exact identifiers; vector retrieval handles semantic similarity; metadata filters enforce scope; reranking improves relevance; provenance determines whether content is eligible as evidence.

QUERY | +--> lexical search +--> vector search +--> metadata/security filter +--> optional KG expansion | +--> merge +--> rerank +--> freshness/authority check +--> evidence pack | vMODEL CONTEXT
tables:
| RAG stage | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Query construction | Use intent/SPEC scope, not arbitrary model instructions |
| Candidate retrieval | Tenant/site/security filters |
| Hybrid merge | Preserve source IDs |
| Reranking | No authority escalation |
| Evidence filter | Authority + validity + freshness |
| Context packing | Token/size budget |
| Generation | Model receives evidence with provenance |
| Post-check | Citations/evidence sufficiency |

sections.content: OWASP's 2025 guidance explicitly treats Vector and Embedding Weaknesses as a security risk and separately warns that prompt injection is not eliminated by RAG. citeturn0search5turn0search6
tables:
| Failure | Problem | AI-ConneX mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong chunk | Relevant document but wrong section | section-aware chunking + reranking |
| Stale procedure | Outdated maintenance step | effective dates + retirement state |
| Vector weakness | Semantically similar but wrong asset | metadata/asset filters |
| Prompt injection in document | Retrieved text gives malicious instruction | retrieved content is data, never authority |
| Cross-tenant retrieval | Information disclosure | pre-retrieval ACL filtering |
| Top-k misses evidence | No supporting passage | hybrid retrieval + query expansion |
| Context overload | Important evidence diluted | rerank + budgeted evidence pack |
| Citation fabrication | Model cites nonexistent source | citation IDs generated by retrieval layer |

sections.content:
The Knowledge Graph represents entities and relationships: plants, lines, machines, sensors, components, failure modes, maintenance procedures, models, datasets, alarms, work orders and dependencies. It answers structural questions that semantic search handles poorly.

Plant  -> contains -> Line  -> contains -> CompressorCompressor  -> hasSensor -> VibrationSensorCompressor  -> hasComponent -> BearingBearing  -> susceptibleTo -> FailureModeFailureMode  -> mitigatedBy -> ProcedureProcedure  -> documentedBy -> DocumentVersion

Graph relationships should carry provenance and, where appropriate, validity intervals. A graph edge is a represented relationship, not proof of causation.
Use stable UIDs and avoid natural-language names as primary identifiers.
tables:
| Entity | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Asset | Plant, Line, Compressor, Pump |
| Component | Bearing, shaft, valve |
| Signal | Vibration, temperature, pressure |
| FailureMode | Bearing wear, imbalance |
| Procedure | Inspection, lubrication |
| Document | Manual/SOP/version |
| Model | Model UID/version |
| Dataset | Manifest/profile/DAG |
| Tool | Alert/create-work-order capability |
| Event | Alarm, maintenance event |

sections.content:
User/Agent Intent      |      +--> KG: "What is connected to COMP-02?"      |       |      |       +--> sensor, component, procedure, model      |      +--> RAG: "What does the approved procedure say?"              |              +--> exact document sections                       |                       +--> combined evidence pack

The graph narrows the search space and supplies structural context; RAG supplies textual evidence. Neither is allowed to silently authorize actions.

Telemetry is fundamentally different from the KB: it describes changing state. AI-ConneX treats telemetry as time-series evidence with timestamp, source, quality, unit, sampling information and freshness.

A stale telemetry value must not be presented as current state. For consequential actions, freshness thresholds belong in the SPEC/policy.
tables:
| Field | Example |
| --- | --- |
| signal_uid | VIB-COMP02-X |
| asset_uid | COMP-02 |
| timestamp | 2026-08-14T10:02:00Z |
| value | 7.3 |
| unit | mm/s |
| quality | GOOD |
| source | PLC/Gateway |
| sampling | 1 Hz |
| ingest_timestamp | ... |
| retention_class | operational |

sections.content:
PLC / SCADA / IoT Gateway        |     protocol adapter        |     message bus        | schema + unit validation        | quality / timestamp check        | time-series store        | feature/window service        | Ground-State / Agent Runtime

For manufacturing architectures, ISO 23247-2 defines a digital-twin reference architecture and ISO 23247-4 addresses information exchange between entities; these are useful standards anchors for separating observable manufacturing elements, digital-twin services and information exchange. citeturn0search1turn0search0

tables:
| Failure | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Clock drift | NTP/time-quality flag + source timestamp |
| Duplicate sample | event ID/window deduplication |
| Out-of-order data | event-time processing |
| Bad sensor | quality flag + plausibility checks |
| Unit mismatch | schema/unit normalization |
| Missing signal | explicit missing state |
| Stale data | freshness gate |
| Gateway outage | buffering + outage state |
| Sensor spoofing | source integrity and anomaly controls |

sections.content:
Models are controlled analytical capabilities. They may be predictive, classificatory, forecasting, anomaly-detection, physics-informed or multimodal. Runtime consumption is through a versioned model contract, not an informal prompt.

MODEL CONTRACTmodel_uidmodel_versioninput_schemaoutput_schematraining_data_refevaluation_refsupported_asset_scopeoperating_limitslatency_budgetuncertainty_fieldsexplanation/evidence fieldsdeployment_status

ML Studio supplies evaluated models and their lineage. The Knowledge layer stores references and documentation; the Runtime verifies the model contract before inference.

tables:
| Failure | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Schema drift | Strict input/output schema |
| Model drift | monitoring + evaluation schedule |
| Out-of-distribution input | domain checks + abstention |
| Low confidence | threshold + escalate |
| Wrong asset family | scope validation |
| Version mismatch | immutable model ref |
| Latency spike | timeout + fallback |
| Prediction hallucination | models are invoked, not generated as text |
| Unexplained prediction | evidence/feature provenance where available |

sections.content:
Allow-list tools per Agent SPEC.

Validate every input against schema.

Bind credentials at gateway, never from model output.

Apply tenant/site/asset authorization.

Require idempotency for write operations.

Use bounded timeout/retry.

Reconcile unknown side-effect status.

Require approval for configured consequence classes.

Capture request/result metadata in audit.

OWASP's 2025 list highlights prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, supply-chain issues, data/model poisoning, improper output handling, excessive agency, vector/embedding weaknesses and unbounded consumption. The architecture maps these risks to source validation, access control, provenance, output schemas, capability limits, retrieval controls and budgets. citeturn0search3turn0search5

tables:
| Observed/anticipated failure | System response |
| --- | --- |
| RAG returns plausible but wrong document | Authority + metadata + hybrid retrieval + reranking |
| Graph gives false causal interpretation | Edge provenance + relationship semantics |
| Telemetry is stale | Freshness gate + quality state |
| Model is used outside evaluated scope | Model scope contract |
| Tool is too powerful | Capability allow-list + gateway |
| Document contains malicious instruction | Data/authority separation |
| Tenant leakage through vector search | Pre-filter ACLs and tenant partitions |
| Tenant leakage through graph | Scope-bound traversal |
| Telemetry leak | Asset/site authorization |
| Embedding poisoning | Source approval, hashes, re-index governance |
| Tool output injects instructions | Tool result treated as untrusted data |
| Evidence too large | Budgeted context + reranking |
| No evidence | Agent abstains/escalates |
| Model confidence high but wrong | Calibration/OOD monitoring + evidence policy |
| Schema drift | Contract/version verification |

sections.content:
This is an engineering readiness/compliance mapping, not legal certification.

NIST's Generative AI Profile is a companion to the AI RMF and is intended to improve trustworthiness considerations throughout AI design, development, use and evaluation. AI-ConneX applies that lifecycle mindset to evidence, models and capabilities. citeturn0search12
tables:
| Control | Implementation evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Governance | KB ownership, SPEC references, model/tool registry |
| Provenance | Document hashes, versions, graph edge provenance, telemetry source IDs |
| Access control | Tenant/site/asset filtering at each plane |
| Data integrity | Checksums, immutable versions, schema validation |
| Freshness | Telemetry timestamps and max-age policy |
| Model governance | Model UID/version/evaluation/scope |
| Tool governance | Capability registry, side-effect class, approval |
| Security | Policy engine, gateway, secrets isolation |
| Traceability | Evidence Pack + Runtime execution trace |
| Human oversight | Approval policy for consequential actions |
| Monitoring | OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs |
| Incident response | Replayable execution and evidence lineage |

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-015 > 34. POC — Compressor Maintenance Knowledge Agent
sections.content:
Objective: answer and act on a compressor-maintenance request using all six planes while proving that the Runtime cannot exceed the Agent SPEC.

Load approved compressor manual v7 and maintenance SOP v4 into the KB.

Build graph entities for Plant-01, COMP-02, bearing, vibration sensor and approved procedures.

Stream vibration/temperature telemetry for COMP-02.

Register ML Studio's evaluated compressor-health model v2.1.0.

Register create_maintenance_alert v1.3 as an INFORM capability.

Create an Agent SPEC limiting evidence to Plant-01 and the compressor family.

Ask Jane: 'Watch COMP-02 and alert maintenance if bearing degradation is likely.'

Runtime resolves graph context and current telemetry.

RAG retrieves the approved bearing procedure.

Model produces a typed health estimate.

Runtime combines prediction + telemetry + graph + procedure evidence.

Tool Gateway creates an alert.

Replay the same event and verify no duplicate alert.

Insert a malicious instruction into a retrieved document and verify it cannot change tool permissions.

Make telemetry stale and verify the Runtime refuses the consequential action.

Attempt an unregistered work-order write tool and verify denial.

Inspect provenance and audit trace.

tables:
| Test | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Source version | Exact document version recorded |
| RAG evidence | Relevant passages + source IDs |
| Graph scope | Only authorized plant/asset entities |
| Telemetry freshness | Stale state blocks configured action |
| Model scope | Correct model version and asset family |
| Tool scope | Only SPEC-listed tool |
| Prompt injection | Retrieved instruction cannot alter authority |
| Duplicate event | Single alert due to idempotency |
| Audit | Evidence and action trace linked to execution |
| Cross-tenant | Request denied |
| Model failure | Declared fallback or escalation |

sections.heading_text: 36. Research References and Why They Matter
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-015 > 36. Research References and Why They Matter
sections.content:
ISO 23247-1:2021 defines general principles for a manufacturing digital-twin framework; ISO 23247-2:2021 provides its reference architecture; ISO 23247-4:2021 specifies technical requirements for information exchange. These support AI-ConneX's separation of assets, services, observable manufacturing elements and information exchange. citeturn0search11turn0search1turn0search0

ISO 23247-5:2026 addresses the digital thread for manufacturing digital twins across lifecycle activities. This is especially relevant to AI-ConneX because Manifest/DAG/Family/model/tool provenance can become part of an industrial digital thread. citeturn0search14

OWASP's LLM guidance identifies prompt injection, vector/embedding weaknesses and excessive agency as material risks for systems combining retrieval and tools. citeturn0search6turn0search5turn0search2

NIST AI RMF's Generative AI Profile provides a cross-sector risk-management reference for trustworthy generative AI design and use. citeturn0search12

OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral instrumentation for traces, metrics and logs, making it a suitable observability baseline for the six-plane foundation and Runtime. citeturn0search18

sections.content: The Runtime consumes these outputs. The next stage is not another unconstrained knowledge stage: it is execution under the Agent SPEC.

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence Pack | Bounded, authorized RAG + graph + telemetry evidence |

sections.heading_text: 38. What This Stage Does NOT Do
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-015 > 38. What This Stage Does NOT Do
sections.content:
It does not authorize industrial actions.

It does not override the Agent SPEC.

It does not treat retrieved text as instructions.

It does not turn telemetry into an action without Runtime/policy checks.

It does not deploy a model; ML Studio owns model training/evaluation.

It does not arbitrarily create tools.

It does not silently cross tenant/site/asset boundaries.

Artifact identity:KB:       DOC-UID:versionRAG index:INDEX-UID:versionGraph:    KG-SNAPSHOT-UID:versionTelemetry schema: SIGNAL-SCHEMA:versionModel:    MODEL-UID:versionTool:     TOOL-UID:versionSPEC:     AGENT-UID:versionExecution records all six references.

This makes an execution reproducible enough to answer: what did the agent know, what state did it observe, which model did it use, what capability did it invoke, and under which contract?
Targets are proposed starting points and should be calibrated against industrial workloads and network topology.
tables:
| Signal | Initial target |
| --- | --- |
| RAG p95 latency | < 800 ms excluding model |
| KG p95 latency | < 300 ms for bounded traversal |
| Telemetry latest lookup | < 200 ms |
| Model inference | Model-specific SLO |
| Tool gateway | Tool-specific SLO |
| Evidence provenance coverage | 100% for production decisions |
| Unauthorized tool calls | 0 permitted |
| Cross-tenant retrieval | 0 permitted |
| Duplicate side effects | 0 permitted after idempotency controls |

sections.content: JANE  -> Intent UID  -> Agent Builder  -> Signed Agent SPEC  -> Agent Runtime       |       +--> Knowledge Base       |      -> authoritative documents       |       +--> RAG       |      -> relevant evidence       |       +--> Knowledge Graph       |      -> structural context       |       +--> Telemetry       |      -> current state       |       +--> Models       |      -> evaluated estimates       |       +--> Tools              -> bounded capabilities                    |                    v               Policy / Approval                    |                    v               Tool Gateway                    |                    v             Industrial Systems                    |             Audit + Visualizer

AI-ConneX should never ask a single component to be simultaneously a database, historian, ontology, predictor and actuator. The six-plane design makes each source good at its own job and forces the Agent Runtime to reconcile them under one explicit contract.

The resulting chain is: Jane expresses intent → Agent Builder formalizes it → Agent SPEC constrains it → Knowledge Foundation grounds it → Agent Runtime reasons and coordinates → Policy authorizes → Tools act → Telemetry observes the result → Audit closes the loop.
